lessons.unit: Unit 1: Next steps and financial capability
lessons.title: Money: payslips, tax and borrowing
objectives: Calculate take-home pay from a gross salary using income tax and National Insurance
Explain how interest, APR and debt work
Describe riba and halal alternatives and make informed financial decisions

keywords.def: pay before deductions
pay after tax and other deductions
a contribution from earnings that funds state benefits
the yearly cost of borrowing as a percentage
interest or increase on a loan, forbidden in Islam

starter: Name two signs of a scam.
What is the difference between income and expenditure?

teach.heading: From gross pay to take-home pay
bullets: Income tax and National Insurance are deducted
Net pay: what you take home
Pension contributions may also be taken
teach.note: Say bismillah. Show a simplified payslip. Explain that tax pays for public services. Use 2026-27 rates in England: personal allowance £12,570; basic rate 20% on income above this up to £50,270; employee National Insurance of 8% on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270 (teachers should check gov.uk for any changes). Link to the Tarbiyyah Compass value of Integrity: honesty in paying what is due. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Worked example: £20,000 a year
teach.note: Walk through the calculation step by step: 7,430 × 0.20 = 1,486; 7,430 × 0.08 = 594.40; 20,000 − 1,486 − 594.40 = 17,919.60. Divide by 12 for about £1,493.30 a month. Pupils should use calculators. Misconception: tax is taken on the whole salary at 20%; only income above the allowance is taxed. Check understanding with a second example in practice.

teach.heading: Borrowing and interest
bullets: APR: compare the true yearly cost
Missed payments harm your credit score
teach.note: Worked example: borrowing £1,000 at 20% APR for one year costs about £200 extra. If only minimum payments are made the cost can rise quickly. Explain credit scores and why they matter for renting and loans. Cite plainly: Qur'an 2:282, which tells believers to write down debts with a fixed term. Link to the hadith that the soul of a believer is held back by their debt until it is paid (Tirmidhi).

teach.heading: Riba and halal alternatives
bullets: Qur'an 2:275: trade is lawful, riba is forbidden
Islamic finance: profit-sharing, cost-plus sale, leasing
teach.note: Cite plainly: Qur'an 2:275-279 on riba. Explain simply how some Islamic products work: a bank buys an item and sells it at an agreed higher price (murabaha); partners share profit and loss (musharakah, mudarabah); leasing (ijara). Note that scholars discuss specific products such as student finance and mortgages; encourage pupils to consult family and qualified scholars for personal decisions. Present scholars' views respectfully.

teach.heading: Spending wisely
bullets: Hadith: asked about wealth, how earned and spent
teach.note: Cite plainly: the hadith that a person will be asked about their wealth, how it was earned and how it was spent (Tirmidhi); and Qur'an 25:67 on moderation. Discuss priorities: rent, food, transport, savings, giving. Ask: ‘What would you cut if income fell by 10%?’ Mention free sources of guidance: MoneyHelper (gov.uk). Link to the Tarbiyyah Compass value of Contentment.

practice: Calculate net pay for a salary of £24,000: tax at 20% and NI at 8% on the amount above £12,570.
You borrow £500 at 24% APR for a year. Approximately how much interest is charged?
Explain the difference between gross and net pay.
independent: Create a monthly budget for someone earning £1,600 net in their first job, including rent, food, transport, savings and sadaqah.
Write a leaflet: ‘Borrowing: what to know before you sign’.
Write a paragraph explaining how Islamic finance differs from interest-based borrowing.
exit: What is the difference between gross and net pay?
Name one halal alternative to an interest-based loan.
lessons.homework: Calculate the take-home pay for a job offering £18,000 a year and write one decision you would make with the money.
lessons.send: SEND: provide a step-by-step calculation template and allow a calculator. EAL: pre-teach finance vocabulary. Stretch: compare the total repaid on a £5,000 loan at 8% and 15% APR over three years.

lessons.title: First aid: CPR on a cushion and the recovery position
lessons.bigQuestion: Most cardiac arrests happen at home. If it happened in your home, would you know what to do?
objectives: To understand how to help an unresponsive casualty: check, call 999, CPR and the recovery position
successCriteria: All: describe the primary survey (danger, response, airway, breathing)
Most: demonstrate CPR rhythm and depth on a cushion
Some: explain when to use the recovery position and when to start CPR
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: the heart and circulatory system

keywords.def: cardiopulmonary resuscitation: chest compressions (and rescue breaths) to keep blood moving
automated external defibrillator: a device that can restart the heart
a safe position for an unresponsive person who is breathing
DRABC: danger, response, airway, breathing, call for help

hook.text: Most cardiac arrests happen at home. If it happened in your home, would you know what to do?
hook.a: Call 999, start CPR, get an AED. Bystander CPR can double the chance of survival.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Whoever saves one life, it is as if he had saved mankind entirely' (al-Ma'idah 5:32). Learning first aid is a way to fulfil this.

starter.q: What does al-Ma'idah 5:32 say about saving a life?
starter.a: It is as if saving all mankind.

teach.heading: Primary survey
bullets: Breathing: look, listen, feel for up to 10 seconds
teach.note: If not breathing normally: call 999 on speaker and start CPR.

teach.heading: CPR (adult)
bullets: Centre of the chest, heel of hand
30 compressions : 2 rescue breaths, or hands-only CPR
teach.note: Practise on a firm cushion on the floor. Never practise compressions on a person.

head: Step
Detail
rows: Speaker on; send someone for an AED
Switch on and follow the voice

teach.heading: Recovery position
bullets: On their side, head tilted back
teach.note: Explain with a diagram; do not demonstrate on another person on camera.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: An adult is unresponsive and not breathing normally. After calling 999 you should...
options: Put them in the recovery position
check.why: No normal breathing means CPR; the recovery position is for someone who is breathing.

practice.q: Practise 30 compressions on a cushion with the teacher's count (100 to 120 a minute).
practice.a: Rhythm kept at about two per second.
practice.model: Teacher demonstrates on a cushion, counting aloud.

independent.q: Core: Sequence cards (pupil PDF): put the steps for an unresponsive casualty in order and say what changes if they are breathing.
independent.a: Danger, response, airway, breathing, 999, CPR and AED; breathing: recovery position.
independent.model: Teacher places the first two cards.

independent.q: Extend: Find where the nearest public AED is to your home (with a parent, using The Circuit or a local map).
Stretch: In the portal response box, explain why hands-only CPR is still worth doing. Start: 'Hands-only CPR...'
independent.a: Hands-only CPR keeps blood with oxygen moving to the brain until help arrives.

exit.q: CPR compression rate? A) 30 a minute B) 100 to 120 a minute C) 200 a minute
Big question: if it happened at home, what would you do first?
exit.a: Check danger and response, call 999, start CPR, get an AED.

lessons.homework: Teach a family member the DRABC steps and the CPR rhythm on a cushion.
lessons.send: SEND: step cards with symbols. EAL: compress, breathe, airway. Stretch: research how an AED decides to shock.

lessons.title: Consent, modesty and the law: protecting dignity and health
objectives: Explain consent and the law, including the age of consent and sexual harassment
Describe, in factual terms, sexual health risks and where to find confidential help
Explain the Islamic teaching that intimacy belongs only within marriage, and how modesty and responsibility protect dignity

keywords.def: freely given agreement that can be withdrawn at any time
an infection that can pass on through sexual contact
unwanted sexual behaviour that makes someone feel uncomfortable or unsafe
keeping intimacy for marriage only, as Islam teaches
being accountable for your choices and their effects

starter: Name two people or services you can ask for help.

teach.heading: Setting the scene
bullets: Factual health and law for Year 11
Taught to boys and girls separately
Parents have seen all the materials
Questions go to the anonymous question box
teach.note: Say bismillah. Teacher note: this lesson is part of RSE taught from an Islamic perspective, to boys and girls separately, in line with the TGA RSHE Policy. Parents are told in advance and can see all materials on the Parent Portal. Pupils learn the law and basic health facts so that they can protect themselves and others and recognise abuse; the Islamic position, that intimacy belongs only within marriage, is taught clearly and without shaming anyone. Follow the policy on any parental withdrawal request. Take questions through the box only. Link to the Tarbiyyah Compass value of Integrity and amanah. Ground rules: right to pass, no personal stories, kindness. Anonymous questions can go to the teacher's question box. If a pupil says anything that worries you, stay calm, do not promise secrecy and follow the Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy: tell the DSL the same day.

teach.heading: Consent and the law
bullets: Consent must be free, informed and can be withdrawn
The age of consent in the UK is 16
Sexual harassment and assault are crimes
Silence, pressure or being intoxicated is not consent
teach.note: Revisit consent from Y9. State the law factually: sexual activity without consent is a crime, and the age of consent is 16 in England and Wales. Explain that pressure, threats and incapacity through alcohol or drugs mean there is no consent. Explain that sexual harassment, including online, is unacceptable. If a pupil is a victim, it is never their fault. Rape Crisis: 0808 500 2222; Childline: 0800 1111.

teach.heading: Islamic teaching on relationships
bullets: Qur'an 17:32: do not go near zina
Qur'an 24:30-31: lower the gaze and guard modesty
Marriage is the context for intimacy
Qur'an 30:21: love and mercy within marriage
teach.note: Cite plainly: Qur'an 17:32 tells believers not to approach unlawful sexual intercourse; 24:30-31 on lowering the gaze and guarding chastity; and 30:21 on love and mercy within marriage. State clearly that the Islamic position is that intimate relationships belong within marriage. Teach respectfully and avoid shaming. Emphasise Allah's mercy, and that anyone who has erred can turn back in repentance. Link to the Tarbiyyah Compass value of Eeman.

teach.heading: Sexual health facts
bullets: STIs can pass on through sexual contact
Some have no symptoms; many are treatable
Abstinence outside marriage is the only certain protection
NHS services are confidential and free
teach.note: Give factual, brief information: STIs such as chlamydia can have no symptoms and can be treated; HIV and hepatitis B are serious but manageable with treatment; testing is available through sexual health clinics and GPs and is confidential. The HPV vaccine is offered through schools in England. Do not teach contraceptive methods. If pupils ask, say that family planning within marriage is a matter scholars have discussed (the narration about ‘azl, Bukhari and Muslim) and that married couples ask a qualified scholar and a doctor. Do not give practical instructions.

teach.heading: Where to get help
bullets: Talk to a parent or trusted adult first
teach.note: Encourage pupils to talk to their parents first. Explain factually that NHS services, including GPs, give confidential advice to young people, though a professional must tell someone if a young person is at risk of harm. Remind pupils that they can talk to the DSL at any time. Revisit the importance of intentions, responsibility and choosing safe paths. Close with a du'a for guidance and purity of heart.

practice: True or false? (a) Consent can be withdrawn at any time. (b) The age of consent in England and Wales is 18. (c) NHS sexual health services are confidential.
Write one sentence explaining why consent cannot be given under pressure.
Name two places a young person can go for confidential health advice.
independent: Create a fact sheet: ‘Know your rights and responsibilities’ with six facts and three services.
Write a response to a friend who says they are being pressured by someone online.
Write a paragraph explaining how Islamic teaching on modesty, marriage and responsibility supports safety and dignity.
exit: Name one person or service you could go to for confidential help.
lessons.homework: Write a paragraph explaining how the law on consent and the Islamic teaching on modesty and marriage each protect people from harm.
lessons.send: SEND: provide fact cards and a simple glossary; offer a private check-in. EAL: pre-teach vocabulary with simple definitions. Stretch: research the Online Safety Act 2023 and how it protects young people from harmful content.

lessons.title: Choking and severe bleeding
lessons.bigQuestion: Someone at the dinner table suddenly cannot speak or cough. What is happening and what will you do?
objectives: To understand how to help someone who is choking or bleeding severely until help arrives
successCriteria: All: tell mild from severe choking
Most: describe back blows and abdominal thrusts in the right order
Some: describe how to control severe bleeding with direct pressure and when to call 999
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: the respiratory system and blood clotting

keywords.def: a blocked airway
firm blows between the shoulder blades to clear a blockage
sharp inward and upward pulls above the navel
pressing firmly on a wound to slow bleeding

hook.text: Someone at the dinner table suddenly cannot speak or cough. What is happening and what will you do?
hook.a: Severe choking: up to 5 back blows, then up to 5 abdominal thrusts, call 999 if not cleared.

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah helps His servant as long as the servant helps his brother' (Muslim). Quick, calm action in an emergency is a way of serving others.

starter.q: When do you use the recovery position?

starter.a: A defibrillator that can restart the heart.

teach.heading: Mild or severe choking?
bullets: Severe: cannot cough, speak or breathe
teach.note: Do not slap the back of someone coughing well.

teach.heading: Severe choking (adult)
bullets: Up to 5 back blows between shoulder blades
teach.note: Explain with a diagram; do not practise thrusts on anyone.

teach.heading: Severe bleeding
bullets: Press firmly on the wound with a clean pad
Keep pressure; add more pads on top
Do not remove objects stuck in a wound
teach.note: Wear gloves if available.

model.problem: A deep cut to the forearm is bleeding heavily.
steps: Check danger; call 999 (or ask someone to)
Press firmly with a clean cloth
Keep pressing; add pads, do not lift to look
Watch for shock: pale, cold, fast breathing

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: A choking adult can still cough strongly. What should you do?
check.why: A strong cough is the best way to clear a mild blockage.

practice.q: Order: abdominal thrusts, encourage cough, back blows, call 999.
practice.a: Encourage cough, back blows, abdominal thrusts, call 999.
practice.model: Teacher orders the steps, explaining the reason for each.

independent.q: Core: Emergency scenarios (pupil PDF): choose the right first aid for four situations.
independent.a: Correct actions for choking and bleeding scenarios.

independent.q: Extend: Check your home first aid kit with a parent and list what is missing.
Stretch: In the portal response box, explain why you should not remove an object stuck in a wound.
independent.a: It may be plugging the wound; removing it can cause heavy bleeding.

exit.q: Severe choking: first action? A) give water B) up to 5 back blows C) wait
Big question: someone at the table cannot speak or cough. What do you do?
exit.a: Back blows, then abdominal thrusts, call 999 if not cleared.

lessons.homework: Show a family member the choking steps on the step card (no practice thrusts).
lessons.send: SEND: step cards with symbols. EAL: choke, bleed, pressure. Stretch: research choking first aid for babies (different steps).

lessons.title: Exam stress: planning the final weeks
lessons.bigQuestion: If you had one hour a day for the next 12 weeks, how would you use it to raise your grades the most?
objectives: To understand how to plan the weeks before the exams so revision is effective and stress is managed

Some: plan for exam-day logistics and how to recover from a bad paper

a real exam paper from an earlier year
the examiner's guide to how marks are given
what to bring, when to arrive and how to stay calm

hook.text: If you had one hour a day for the next 12 weeks, how would you use it to raise your grades the most?
hook.a: Target weakest topics with retrieval and past paper questions, marked with mark schemes.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah' (Al 'Imran 3:159). Plan well, work steadily, make du'a and then trust Allah with the result (tawakkul).

starter.a: The examiner's guide to awarding marks.

Private candidates at a booked centre
